newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CLEMENTE LOOKS TO SWAMP MALTA IN 50TH GAME IN CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CLEMENTE LOOKS TO SWAMP MALTA IN 50TH GAME IN CHARGE.

text.p: Javier Clemente can reasonably expect to celebrate his 50th game in charge of the Spanish national side on Wednesday with victory in a World Cup qualifier over group six strugglers Malta.
Clemente knows any other result would be a disaster and that a goal avalanche would significantly boost Spain's chances of winning the group, which they lead by one point from Yugoslavia.
Penalty shoot-outs discounted, Spain are unbeaten since summer 1994, while Malta have not scored in their four group games and have conceded 21 goals.

But the Spanish coach is conscious that the backbone of his team -- seven Barcelona players -- has been badly affected by weekend league action which left the club eight points behind arch-rivals Real Madrid.
"They won't be so happy...but those from Real will be," Clemente said.

Clemente may substitute or even leave out three Barcelona players -- defenders Abelardo Fernandez and Miguel Angel Nadal and utility man Luis Enrique. They would face suspension for April's vital match in Yugoslavia if they picked up yellow cards against Malta.
Another Barcelona player, defender Albert Ferrer, has had to pull out of the squad after receiving up a knock in Sunday's 2-0 defeat at Espanyol.
Ferrer will be replaced by a midfielder, Deportivo Coruna's Armandao Alvarez, who won his first cap in December's 3-0 win in Malta.
Julen Guerrero scored all three goals in that match and is again likely to start on Wednesday. The Athletic Bilbao striker is one Clemente's biggest fans.
"His trajectory is fantastic," Guerrero said. "He just needs to confirm it all in a final phase."

Elimination in the quarter-finals of the 1994 World Cup and the 1996 European championship account for two out of three defeats in Clemente's 49 matches in charge. Both were games which Spain should have won.
